newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin calls in army to help combat crime.
newsitem.headline: Benin calls in army to help combat crime.

text.p: Heavily armed military units have joined the police and the gendamerie to combat a rising wave of violent crime in Benin, witnesses said on Saturday.
An army officer described the operation as "patrol and reconnaissance" duty following an order from Interior Minister Theophile N'Dah on Friday.
Several army units were involved in day and night patrols in different parts of the West African country.
Police have reported a sharp rise in holdups and killings by armed men across the country since last month.
Two Lebanese nationals were shot dead in central Cotonou on August 12 and a teenaged girl was gunned down the same day outside Cotonou's central market.

Since then a shopkeeper was robbed and hacked to death in Lokossa, 100 km (60 miles) from Cotonou, three separate motorcyclists were shot at on a highway outside Cotonou in a two-hour period while three attacks on taxi drivers were reported in Abomey, 150 km (90 miles) northwest of Benin.

Police and gendamerie operations in the past week led to about 400 arrests, some of them foreigners who were later deported, police said. Benin shares frontiers with Nigeria, Togo, Burkina Faso and Niger.
